messages:
maria: Heads-up — our repo-template tests started failing on GH Actions when importing @redwood/inference-js in a page test. Works locally with Node runner, fails in Vitest (jsdom) on CI.

maria: Failure: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module (points at node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs)

kevin: Sounds like the test runner is resolving to the CJS entry. What's inside package.json exports and your vitest config?

maria: package.json has both "main": "dist/index.cjs" and "module": "dist/index.mjs" and an "exports" map. vitest config is basically default; test environment jsdom.

dave: Common pattern: Vite sometimes bundles deps differently in deps optimization vs ssr. Try vitest: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference-js'] } } or in vite: { ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/inference-js'] } } to force ESM build through esbuild.

maria: tried noExternal — progress, but now runtime fails with ReferenceError: self is not defined coming from a small runtime check in SDK that assumes worker/global scope. It runs at import-time.

jen: Ugh import-time side effects are the worst for tests. Two approaches: (1) SDK changes to lazy-evaluate environment probes (wrap in function), (2) tests mock the package to avoid executing the probe. For integration tests you might need option 1.

kevin: For immediate CI unblocking, vi.mock('@redwood/inference-js', async () => {
  const actual = await vi.importActual('@redwood/inference-js')
  return { ...actual, createClient: () => ({ generate: () => 'mocked' }) }
}) at top of test — but note importActual may still evaluate module. Safer is to provide a manual mock object.

maria: manual mock worked. But wanted to run some flow tests that exercise stream helpers. Can't mock all of that.

dave: SDK runtime change suggestion: use typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window : globalThis. That avoids ReferenceError during property access. Also guard with try/catch around any constructor checks. Non-breaking if done carefully.

jen: On the Jest side, people should add transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/inference-js)'] and use babel-jest or ts-jest to compile ESM deps. For ts-jest, set useESM: true and extensions .mts/.ts handling.

maria: Another gotcha: TS imports and mocking. If consumers have esModuleInterop:false, default import syntax breaks. In tests we had to switch to `import * as rwi from '@redwood/inference-js'` and then `vi.spyOn(rwi, 'createClient').mockImplementation(...)` to preserve typings.

kevin: Add to the sample app README: recommended vitest.config.ts snippet and mock helpers. Example snippet I plan to add:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference-js'] },
    globals: true,
  },
  optimizeDeps: { include: ['@redwood/inference-js'] },
  ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/inference-js'] },
})
```
Make sure to note that inline/noExternal solves ESM dep transform for Vitest v0.34+.

dave: Also call out node/ci differences: CI uses Node 18 with --experimental-fetch in one workflow, that affects fetch detection. Recommend tests to `globalThis.fetch = globalThis.fetch || (() => {})` in setupFiles before importing SDK.

jen: Typing notes: when writing mocks for TS, export `type Client = ReturnType<typeof createClient>` in SDK types so tests can do `const client = {} as Client` for typed fakes. That avoids `any` creeping in.

maria: I'll open a PR in repo-template with example vitest/jest configs + a small `test-helpers/mock-rwi.ts` that exports a typed fake client.

ci-bot: CI label added: devex/esmodules-test-failures (#4012).

kevin: Action items: (1) DevEx — add docs + example configs, (2) SDK — guard global checks and add a test-safe helper export, (3) Repo-template — include setupFiles that mock fetch/self for CI. I'll create issues and link them.

maria: Thanks all — manual mock + inline/noExternal unblocked our pipeline. Will paste exact config in #devex once PRs land. :sparkles:
